title: IRoC – Indian Rover Challenge
description: A national-level autonomous rover competition simulating Mars exploration tasks including terrain traversal, object detection, waypoint navigation, and robotic arm operations.
detailedDescription:
The Indian Rover Challenge (IRoC) is a prestigious intercollegiate competition that tasks student teams with building Mars analogue rovers capable of completing a series of autonomous and semi-autonomous mission tasks in simulated extraterrestrial terrain.

Competition tasks typically include:
- Autonomous traversal across rocky, sandy, and uneven terrain
- GPS waypoint navigation with obstacle avoidance
- Object detection and retrieval using a robotic arm
- Precision landing or docking on marked targets
- Science task simulations involving soil sampling or instrument deployment

Key technical challenges:
- Building a chassis robust enough for Mars-analogue terrain (rocks, slopes, loose soil)
- Integrating autonomous navigation with real-time sensor feedback
- Developing a functional robotic arm with adequate degrees of freedom
- Ensuring reliable communication between the rover and ground station
- Managing power efficiently across motors, computing, and sensors

Relevance to our teams:
- TerronX competes directly in IRoC with its 6-wheel rocker-bogie rover
- ArionX's autonomous drone capabilities align with IRoC aerial sub-tasks
- Builds cross-disciplinary skills in mechanical design, embedded systems, ROS, and computer vision

Impact:
IRoC pushes student teams to engineer systems at the intersection of mechanical robustness, software intelligence, and real-world reliability — mirroring the challenges faced by actual planetary exploration programs like NASA's Mars 2020 mission.

title: TerronX Autonomous Rover
description: A six-wheeled autonomous ground rover with rocker-bogie suspension, LiDAR-based obstacle avoidance, and PID-controlled navigation for IRC/IRoC competition terrain.
detailedDescription:
TerronX is an autonomous rover built for competition environments featuring rocky terrain, sand, and slopes. It draws inspiration from NASA Mars rover designs, adapting proven mechanical and software principles for IRC and IRoC challenges.

How it works:
- Rocker-bogie suspension keeps all six wheels in ground contact across uneven surfaces
- DC geared motors with L298N drivers provide independent wheel torque control
- RPLIDAR A1 scans the surroundings to build an occupancy grid for path planning
- Raspberry Pi runs the navigation stack (ROS-based) while Arduino handles low-level motor control

System capabilities:
- 6-wheel rocker-bogie drivetrain with skid steering for rough terrain traversal
- LiDAR + ultrasonic sensor fusion for obstacle detection up to 4m
- Waypoint navigation with A* path planning and real-time obstacle avoidance
- IMU (MPU6050) for orientation tracking and slope detection
- LiPo battery with buck converter power distribution for all subsystems

Impact:
TerronX provides a robust, competition-ready rover platform capable of navigating challenging outdoor terrain autonomously, serving as a foundation for Mars rover analogue tasks and autonomous field robotics research.

title: ArionX Autonomous Drone
description: A quadcopter UAV with PID-based flight stabilization, GPS waypoint navigation, and computer vision for autonomous target detection and precision landing using ArUco markers.
detailedDescription:
ArionX is an autonomous aerial robot designed for both outdoor GPS-guided missions and indoor vision-based tasks. It combines a tuned flight controller stack with onboard computing to enable fully autonomous operation.

How it works:
- Brushless BLDC motors with ESCs drive four propellers in an X-frame configuration
- Flight controller runs a PID loop at 4000+ Hz to maintain stable attitude across all three axes
- GPS and IMU provide outdoor positioning; camera-based ArUco detection handles indoor precision tasks
- Raspberry Pi onboard computer runs OpenCV pipelines for real-time marker detection and landing

System capabilities:
- ArduPilot or PX4 firmware for flexible autonomous flight modes
- GPS waypoint navigation with failsafe return-to-launch
- ArUco marker detection for precision autonomous landing
- LiPo battery system with BEC voltage regulation for all peripherals
- RC transmitter/receiver link with telemetry for ground monitoring

Impact:
ArionX demonstrates end-to-end autonomous aerial capability — from motor-level PID stabilization to high-level vision-guided landing — making it a strong base for IRoC and search-and-rescue UAV applications.

title: HydronX Underwater Robot
description: An autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) built for deep-sea navigation, object detection, and competition tasks using thrusters, sonar, and pressure-aware waterproof systems.
detailedDescription:
HydronX is an autonomous underwater robot engineered for structured aquatic environments and competition tasks such as RoboSub. It integrates multi-axis thruster propulsion, sensor fusion, and sealed electronics to operate reliably at depth.

How it works:
- Brushless thrusters (Blue Robotics T200) arranged in a 6-DOF configuration for full directional control
- Sonar and cameras work together to detect colored buoys, gates, and target objects
- Pressure sensors continuously track depth to maintain target altitude
- IMU-based orientation feedback feeds into closed-loop control for stable maneuvering

System capabilities:
- 6-thruster propulsion for forward, lateral, and vertical movement
- Vision system using underwater cameras with color correction for target detection
- Acoustic sonar (Blue Robotics Ping) for obstacle ranging up to 30m
- Waterproof enclosures with O-ring seals and cable penetrators rated to 15m depth
- LiPo battery power system with regulated supply rails for all onboard electronics

Impact:
HydronX serves as a capable platform for underwater autonomy research and RoboSub-style competitions, demonstrating thruster control, sensor integration, and robust waterproofing in a challenging aquatic environment.

title: KinetonX Autonomous Racing Robot
description: A high-speed autonomous racing robot featuring line following, PID control, and real-time track navigation for competitive corridor racing.
detailedDescription:
KinetonX is an autonomous racing robot engineered for speed and precision on structured tracks. It combines sensor fusion, closed-loop control, and onboard processing to navigate racing lines at high speeds with minimal deviation.

How it works:
- IR sensor array continuously detects the racing line position
- PID controller computes real-time steering and speed corrections
- Weighted average algorithm determines exact line offset for smooth curve handling
- Brushless motors driven by ESCs deliver high-torque, high-speed propulsion

System capabilities:
- Line following using multi-channel IR sensor array (QTR-8A or equivalent)
- PID-based steering and speed control for stable high-speed navigation
- Brushless DC motor drivetrain with ESC for rapid acceleration
- LiPo battery power system with regulated supply for electronics
- Arduino-based control pipeline for reliable real-time behavior

Impact:
KinetonX serves as a competitive base platform for autonomous racing challenges, demonstrating the integration of sensor feedback, control theory, and efficient power management in a high-speed mobile robot.

title: Automated Bot
description: A wall-following autonomous bot that maintains distance, detects parcel boxes, counts laps via IR strip sensing, and displays stats on an LCD.
detailedDescription:
This project is an autonomous wall-following robot designed for navigation and tracking tasks in controlled corridors. It uses closed-loop feedback to hold a stable offset from walls while scanning for marked objects.

How it works:
- Dual Sharp sensors continuously measure wall distance
- The controller computes correction values in real time
- IR strip detection marks lap completion points
- Object checks are logged while moving through each segment

System capabilities:
- Distance control using dual Sharp sensors
- Lap tracking through IR strip detection
- Real-time counters shown on a 16x2 LCD
- Arduino-based control pipeline for reliable behavior

Impact:
This bot serves as a practical base for warehouse-path prototypes and autonomous corridor navigation tasks where repeatability and clear monitoring are essential.

title: Mark 1.6
description: A fully wireless Bluetooth-controlled robotic arm mounted on a 4WD chassis, built with 3D-printed components and NRF communication modules.
detailedDescription:
Mark 1.6 combines mobility and manipulation in one platform. A 3D-printed robotic arm is integrated with a 4WD base, enabling both movement and pick-and-place style operations through wireless control.

Design approach:
- Compact arm geometry optimized for lightweight movement
- Wireless stack to separate control logic from hardware wiring constraints
- Chassis-arm integration tuned for center-of-mass stability

System capabilities:
- Bluetooth and NRF-based wireless command flow
- 3D-printed arm structure for rapid prototyping
- 4WD chassis for stable movement
- Practical platform for control and mechatronics testing

Why it matters:
This platform is ideal for demonstrating coordinated locomotion + manipulation, which is a core requirement in field robotics and assisted automation systems.

title: Line Follower Bot
description: A mobile robot that detects and follows floor tracks using IR sensors, onboard processing, and motor driver control for autonomous path following.
detailedDescription:
The Line Follower Bot is built for autonomous path tracing on high-contrast tracks. Sensor readings are continuously processed to adjust wheel speed and steering in real time.

Control workflow:
- IR array samples line position at high frequency
- Error between centerline and robot orientation is computed
- Motor PWM values are adjusted dynamically to reduce drift
- Smoother turns are achieved through tuned correction thresholds

System capabilities:
- IR sensor array for line detection
- Fast motor correction loop for stable tracking
- Embedded control for route adherence
- Competition-friendly design for speed and precision

Learning outcome:
This project provides strong fundamentals in sensor-based feedback, tuning, and real-time embedded decision-making.

title: PlutoX
description: An open-source nano drone with Wi-Fi camera support, manual app control, and ROS-based scripting for computer-vision and automation workflows.
detailedDescription:
PlutoX is a lightweight programmable drone used to explore ROS workflows, image processing, and autonomous flight logic. It supports manual control as well as script-driven behavior.

Development focus:
- Rapid integration between camera stream and perception modules
- Script-based mission logic for waypoint and task automation
- Human-in-loop fallback for safer real-world testing

System capabilities:
- 720p camera stream for CV experiments
- ROS integration for automation pipelines
- Manual app control for field testing
- Suitable for surveillance and mapping prototypes

Future scope:
The same platform can be extended to traffic analytics, search-and-assist scenarios, and autonomous monitoring pipelines.

title: 3D Printing
description: Additive manufacturing workflows used to convert digital models into physical prototypes by depositing material layer by layer.
detailedDescription:
This initiative focuses on additive manufacturing for rapid robotics prototyping. Digital CAD models are converted into physical components through layered deposition.

Workflow:
- CAD design and tolerance validation
- Slicer configuration for layer quality and infill strength
- Iterative prints with fit and load testing
- Revision cycle based on assembly performance

System capabilities:
- Faster iteration for custom robot parts
- Reduced fabrication cost for small batches
- Better fit-checking before final builds
- Supports arm joints, mounts, brackets, and enclosures

Practical value:
3D printing significantly shortens build cycles and enables low-cost experimentation for student-led hardware innovation.

title: Self Balancing Bot
description: An inverted-pendulum robot that stays upright by driving its wheels in the direction of tilt using MPU6050 sensor feedback and control logic.
detailedDescription:
The Self Balancing Bot demonstrates inverted-pendulum stabilization. Sensor fusion and control tuning are used to keep the center of mass aligned above the wheel axis.

Control pipeline:
- IMU data is sampled for tilt and angular velocity
- Error from target upright angle is calculated continuously
- Motor commands are generated through tuned feedback gains
- Disturbance recovery is improved via iterative calibration

System capabilities:
- MPU6050-based tilt sensing
- Real-time correction through motor drive
- PID-style control behavior for stability
- Strong learning platform for dynamics and control theory

Engineering value:
This project is a compact and powerful testbed for understanding stability, control loops, and real-time corrective actuation.

title: Radar Navigation
description: A marine-navigation study project focused on radar-based vessel detection, tracking, and positioning using X-band and S-band systems.
detailedDescription:
Radar Navigation is a domain study project centered on vessel identification and safe route awareness in maritime environments. It compares X-band and S-band behavior across weather and visibility conditions.

Study coverage:
- Radar-based target detection and echo interpretation
- Relative motion understanding for collision avoidance
- Environmental influence on signal reliability
- Practical differences between X-band and S-band operation

Key highlights:
- Vessel tracking and positioning concepts
- X-band for sharper target resolution
- S-band for reliability in rain and fog
- Safety-focused interpretation aligned with navigation rules

Outcome:
The project builds a clear conceptual base for safe marine navigation, situational awareness, and radar-assisted decision support.

title: Hexapod
description: A six-legged robotic platform designed for stable multi-axis motion using Arduino Nano, SG90 servos, PCA9685 driver, and 3D-printed parts.
detailedDescription:
Hexapod is a six-legged walking robot created for stable locomotion and gait experimentation. Its modular frame and servo architecture support repeatable motion studies.

Locomotion strategy:
- Coordinated leg sequencing for tripod-style movement
- Servo timing optimization for smooth transitions
- Balance maintenance during turns and uneven motion
- Mechanical tuning for reduced wobble and energy loss

Key highlights:
- 6-DOF locomotion behavior with gait patterns
- Arduino Nano + PCA9685 servo orchestration
- SG90 servo-based joint control
- 3D-printed chassis for lightweight structure

Why this project matters:
It introduces core concepts of legged robotics, gait planning, and motion control beyond conventional wheeled platforms.

title: Air Quality Monitoring Drone
description: A manually controlled drone that captures atmospheric gas data via MQ2 and uploads telemetry to Firebase using ESP8266 for remote monitoring.
detailedDescription:
This drone platform is designed for air-quality monitoring in zones that are hard to inspect manually. It captures gas concentration data and pushes live telemetry to cloud storage.

Operational flow:
- Drone captures region-specific air samples during flight
- MQ2 sensor readings are processed onboard
- ESP8266 publishes timestamped values to Firebase
- Remote dashboard enables live monitoring and analysis

Key highlights:
- MQ2 sensing for gases like LPG, methane, and CO
- ESP8266 pipeline for Firebase updates
- Field-deployable multirotor stack for data capture
- Useful for urban monitoring and hazardous area checks

Deployment value:
The system supports data-driven environmental checks for campuses, industrial zones, and difficult-to-access locations.
